segs.e: Linked Discourses 2.1
1. Chapter One
With Kassapa (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho kassapo devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kassapo devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Kassapa, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “bhikkhuṁ bhagavā pakāsesi, no ca bhikkhuno anusāsan”ti.
segs.e: “The Buddha has revealed the mendicant, but not his instructions to a mendicant.”
“Well then, Kassapa, clarify this matter yourself.”
“You should all train <j>to learn well-spoken words,
to attend closely to ascetics,
to sit alone in hidden places,
and to settle the mind.”
That is what the godling Kassapa said,
and the Teacher concurred.

segs.p: Atha kho kassapo devaputto “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Kassapa, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.
Linked Discourses 2.2
Chapter One
With Kassapa (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kassapo devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Kassapa spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“If a mendicant is a meditator, freed in mind,
and if they desire the heart’s fulfillment—
having known the arising and passing of the world,
good-hearted, independent, that is their reward.”
Linked Discourses 2.3
Chapter One
With Māgha
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho māgho devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Māgha, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho māgho devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: and addressed the Buddha in verse:
“When what is slain do you sleep at ease?
When what is slain is there no sorrow?
What is the one thing
whose killing you approve?”
“When anger’s slain you sleep at ease.
When anger’s slain there is no sorrow.
Anger has a poisonous root
and a sweet tip, O Smiter of the Constrictor.
The noble ones praise its killing,
for when it’s slain there is no sorrow.”
Linked Discourses 2.4
Chapter One
With Maghada
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho māgadho devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Maghada addressed the Buddha in verse:
“How many lamps are there
that light up the world?
We’ve come to ask the Buddha;
how are we to understand this?”
“There are four lamps in the world,
a fifth is not found.
The sun blazes by day,
the moon radiates at night,
while a fire illuminates both
by day and by night.
But a Buddha is the best of blazes:
this is the supreme radiance.”
Linked Discourses 2.5
Chapter One
With Dāmali
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho dāmali devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Dāmali, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho dāmali devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“This is what should be done by a brahmin:
unrelenting striving.
Then, with the giving up of sensual pleasures,
they won’t hope to be reborn.”
“The brahmin has nothing left to do,”
said the Buddha to Dāmali,
“for they’ve completed their task.
So long as a personage fails to gain a footing in the river,
they swim with every limb.
But someone who has gained a footing <j>and stands on dry land
need not swim, <j>for they have reached the far shore.
Dāmali, this is a simile for the brahmin,
alert, a meditator who has ended defilements.
Since they’ve reached the end of rebirth and death,
they need not swim, <j>for they have reached the far shore.”
Linked Discourses 2.6
Chapter One
With Kāmada
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kāmado devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Kāmada said to the Buddha,
“It’s too hard, Blessed One! It’s just too hard!”
“They do it even though it’s hard,”
said the Buddha to Kāmada,
“the stable trainees with ethics, and immersion.
For one who has entered the homeless life,
contentment brings happiness.”
“Such contentment, Blessed One, is hard to find.”
“They find it even though it’s hard,”
said the Buddha to Kāmada,
“those who love to settle the mind;
whose minds love to meditate
day and night.”
“But it’s hard, Blessed One, to immerse this mind in samādhi.”
“They become immersed in samādhi <j>even though it’s hard,”
said the Buddha to Kāmada,
“those who love calming the faculties.
Having cut through the net of Death,
the noble ones, Kāmada, go on their way.”
“But this path, Blessed One, is rough and hard to travel.”
“Though it’s rough, hard to travel,
the noble ones, Kāmada, go on their way.
The ignoble fall headfirst
on a rough path.
But the path of the noble ones is smooth,
for the noble ones are smooth amid the rough.”
Linked Discourses 2.7
Chapter One
With Pañcālacaṇḍa
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho pañcālacaṇḍo devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Pañcālacaṇḍa spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“The opening amid confinement
was discovered by the Buddha of vast intelligence,
who awakened to absorption,
the sage, the solitary boss bull.”
“Even amid confinement they understand,”
said the Buddha to Pañcālacaṇḍa,
“the principle for attaining extinguishment.
Those who have acquired mindfulness
are perfectly serene in samādhi.”
Linked Discourses 2.8
Chapter One
With Tāyana
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho tāyano devaputto purāṇatitthakaro abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Tāyana, formerly a religious founder, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho tāyano devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:
“Cut the stream, striving!
Cast aside sensual pleasures, brahmin.
A sage who doesn’t give up sensual pleasures
is not reborn in a unified state.
If one is to do what should be done,
one should staunchly strive.
For the life gone forth when laxly led
just stirs up dust all the more.
A bad deed is better left undone,
for it will plague you later on.
A good deed is better done,
one that does not plague you.
When kusa grass is wrongly grasped
it only cuts the hand.
So too, the ascetic life, when wrongly taken,
drags you to hell.
Any lax act,
any corrupt observance,
or suspicious spiritual life,
is not very fruitful.”
That is what the godling Tāyana said.

segs.p: idaṁ vatvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened.

segs.p: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ tāyano nāma devaputto purāṇatitthakaro abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, tonight, the glorious godling Tāyana, formerly a religious founder, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, tāyano devaputto mama santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: and recited these verses in my presence.” The Buddha repeated the verses in full, adding:

segs.p: Idamavoca, bhikkhave, tāyano devaputto, idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
segs.e: “That is what the godling Tāyana said. Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right side, before vanishing right there.
Mendicants, learn the verses of Tāyana!
Memorize the verses of Tāyana!
Remember the verses of Tāyana!
These verses are beneficial and relate to the fundamentals of the spiritual life.”
Linked Discourses 2.9
Chapter One
The Moon
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena candimā devaputto rāhunā asurindena gahito hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Moon God had been seized by Rāhu, lord of titans.

segs.p: Atha kho candimā devaputto bhagavantaṁ anussaramāno tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Moon God, recollecting the Buddha, at that time spoke this verse:
“Homage to you, Buddha, hero!
You’re free in every way.
I’ve wandered into confinement:
be my refuge!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā candimaṁ devaputtaṁ ārabbha rāhuṁ asurindaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha addressed Rāhu in verse concerning the Moon God:
“The Moon God has gone for refuge
to the Realized One, the perfected one.
The Buddhas have compassion for the world—
so Rāhu, release the Moon!”

segs.p: Atha kho rāhu asurindo candimaṁ devaputtaṁ muñcitvā taramānarūpo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā saṁviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then Rāhu, having released the Moon, rushed to see Vepacitti, lord of titans and stood to one side, shocked and awestruck.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho rāhuṁ asurindaṁ vepacitti asurindo gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Vepacitti addressed him in verse:
“Why the rush?
Rāhu, you released the Moon
and came here looking like you’re in shock:
why do you stand there so scared?”
“My head would have exploded in seven pieces,
I would have found no happiness in life,
if, when enchanted by the Buddha’s verse,
I had not released the Moon.”
Linked Discourses 2.10
Chapter One
The Sun
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sūriyo devaputto rāhunā asurindena gahito hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Sun God had been seized by Rāhu, lord of titans.

segs.p: Atha kho sūriyo devaputto bhagavantaṁ anussaramāno tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Sun God, recollecting the Buddha, at that time spoke this verse:
“Homage to you, Buddha, hero!
You’re free in every way.
I’ve wandered into confinement:
be my refuge!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sūriyaṁ devaputtaṁ ārabbha rāhuṁ asurindaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha addressed Rāhu in verse concerning the Sun God:
“The Sun God has gone for refuge
to the Realized One, the perfected one.
The Buddhas have compassion for the world—
so Rāhu, release the Sun!
He is a beacon in the darkness,
the dazzling sun, circle of awesome might.
Rāhu, do not swallow him as he traverses the sky.
Rāhu, release my offspring, the Sun!”

segs.p: Atha kho rāhu asurindo sūriyaṁ devaputtaṁ muñcitvā taramānarūpo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā saṁviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then Rāhu, having released the Sun, rushed to see Vepacitti, lord of titans and stood to one side, shocked and awestruck.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho rāhuṁ asurindaṁ vepacitti asurindo gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Vepacitti addressed him in verse:
“Why the rush?
Rāhu, you released the Sun
and came here looking like you’re in shock:
why do you stand there so scared?”
“My head would have exploded in seven pieces,
I would have found no joy in life,
if, when enchanted by the Buddha’s verse,
I had not released the Sun.”
Linked Discourses 2.11
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Candimasa
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho candimaso devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Candimasa, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho candimaso devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“Like deer in a mosquito-free marsh,
they will reach a safe place
having entered the absorptions,
unified, alert, and mindful.”
“Like fish when the net is cut,
they will reach the far shore
having entered the absorptions,
diligent, with strife discarded.”
Linked Discourses 2.12
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Vishnu

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho veṇḍu devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Vishnu spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“Happy are the men
who pay homage to the Holy One!
They apply themselves to Gotama’s instructions,
diligently training.”
“Those who practice absorption <j>in accord with the training”,
said the Buddha to Vishnu,
“in the way of teaching I’ve proclaimed,
diligent while there is still time;
they won’t fall under the sway of Death.”
Linked Discourses 2.13
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Dīghalaṭṭhi
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho dīghalaṭṭhi devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ veḷuvanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Dīghalaṭṭhi, lighting up the entire Bamboo Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho dīghalaṭṭhi devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“If a mendicant is a meditator, freed in mind,
and if they desire the heart’s fulfillment—
having known the arising and passing of the world,
good-hearted, independent, that is their reward.”
Linked Discourses 2.14
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Nandana

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho nandano devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Nandana addressed the Buddha in verse:
“I ask you, Gotama, whose wisdom is vast,
the Blessed One <j>of unhindered knowledge and vision.
What sort do they call ethical?
What sort do they call wise?
What sort lives on after transcending suffering?
What sort is worshiped by the deities?”
“Someone who is ethical, wise, evolved,
becomes serene, loving absorption, mindful,
who’s gotten rid of and given up all sorrows,
with defilements ended, they bear their final body.
That sort they call ethical.
That sort they call wise.
That sort lives on after transcending suffering.
That sort is worshiped by the deities.”
Linked Discourses 2.15
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Candana

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho candano devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Candana addressed the Buddha in verse:
“Who here crosses the flood,
tireless all day and night?
Who, not standing and unsupported,
does not sink in the deep?”
“Someone who is always endowed with ethics,
wise and serene,
energetic and resolute,
crosses the flood so hard to cross.
Someone who desists from sensual perception,
has moved past the fetter of form,
and has finished with relishing and greed
does not sink in the deep.”
Linked Discourses 2.16
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Vāsudatta

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho vāsudatto devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Vāsudatta spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“Like they’re struck by a sword,
like their head was on fire,
a mendicant should wander mindful,
to give up sensual desire.”
“Like they’re struck by a sword,
like their head was on fire,
a mendicant should wander mindful,
to give up substantialist view.”
Linked Discourses 2.17
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Subrahmā

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho subrahmā devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Subrahmā addressed the Buddha in verse:
“This mind is always anxious,
this mind is always stressed
about stresses that haven’t arisen
and those that have.
If there is a state free of anxiety,
please answer my question.”
“Not without understanding and fervor,
not without restraining the sense faculties,
not without letting go of everything,
do I see safety for living creatures.”
That is what the Buddha said. …
The godling vanished right there.
Linked Discourses 2.18
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Kakudha
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sākete viharati añjanavane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāketa in the deer park at the Añjana Wood.

segs.p: Atha kho kakudho devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ añjanavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kakudho devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Kakudha, lighting up the entire Añjana Wood, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,
“Do you delight, ascetic?”
“What have I gained, sir?”
“Well then, ascetic, do you sorrow?”
“What have I lost, sir?”

segs.p: “Tena hi, samaṇa, neva nandasi na ca socasī”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, ascetic, do you neither delight nor sorrow?”
“Yes, sir.”
“I hope you’re not gloomy, mendicant,
I hope that delight isn’t found in you.
I hope that discontent doesn’t
overwhelm you as you sit alone.”
“I’m genuinely not gloomy, spirit,
and no delight is found in me.
And also discontent doesn’t
overwhelm me as I sit alone.”
“How are you not gloomy, mendicant?
How is delight not found in you?
How does discontent not
overwhelm you as you sit alone?”
“Delight is born from gloom,
gloom is born from delight;
sir, you should know me as
a mendicant free of delight and gloom.”
“After a long time I see
a brahmin fully quenched.
A mendicant free of delight and gloom,
he has crossed over clinging to the world.”
Linked Discourses 2.19
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Uttara
At Rājagaha.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho uttaro devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Uttara spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“This life, so very short, is led onward.
One led on to old age has no shelter.
Seeing this peril in death,
do good deeds that bring you joy.”
“This life, so very short, is led onward.
One led on to old age has no shelter.
Seeing this peril in death,
a seeker of peace would drop the world’s bait.”
Linked Discourses 2.20
2. With Anāthapiṇḍika
With Anāthapiṇḍika

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Anāthapiṇḍika recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:
“This is indeed that Jeta’s Grove,
frequented by the Saṅgha of seers,
where the King of Dhamma stayed:
it brings me joy!
Deeds, knowledge, and principle;
ethical conduct, an excellent livelihood;
by these are mortals purified,
not by clan or wealth.
That’s why an astute person,
seeing what’s good for themselves,
would examine the teaching rationally,
that’s how they become purified in that.
Sāriputta is full of wisdom,
ethics, and peace.
Even a mendicant who has crossed over
might at best equal him.”
That is what the godling Anāthapiṇḍika said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññataro devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, tonight, a certain glorious godling, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, so devaputto mama santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: and recited these verses in my presence.” The Buddha then repeated the verses in full.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “so hi nūna, bhante, anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto bhavissati.
segs.e: “Sir, that godling must surely have been Anāthapiṇḍika.

segs.p: Anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati āyasmante sāriputte abhippasanno ahosī”ti.
segs.e: For the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was devoted to Venerable Sāriputta.”

segs.p: “Sādhu sādhu, ānanda, yāvatakaṁ kho, ānanda, takkāya pattabbaṁ anuppattaṁ taṁ tayā.
segs.e: “Good, good, Ānanda. You’ve reached the logical conclusion, as far as logic goes.
For that was indeed the godling Anāthapiṇḍika.”
Linked Discourses 2.21
3. Various Sectarians
With Shiva
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho sivo devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Shiva, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho sivo devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
things get better, not worse.
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
wisdom is gained—but not from anyone else.
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you grieve not among the grieving.
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you dazzle among your relatives.
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
sentient beings go to a good place.
Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
sentient beings live happily.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sivaṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha replied to Shiva in verse:
“Associate only with the virtuous!
Try to get close to the virtuous!
Understanding the true teaching of the good,
you’re released from all suffering.”
Linked Discourses 2.22
3. Various Sectarians
With Khema

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho khemo devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Khema recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:
“Fools and simpletons behave
like their own worst enemies,
doing wicked deeds
that ripen as bitter fruit.
It’s not good to do a deed
that plagues you later on,
for which you weep and wail,
as its effect stays with you.
It is good to do a deed
that doesn’t plague you later on,
that gladdens and cheers,
as its effect stays with you.”
“As a precaution, you should do
what you know is for your own welfare.
A thinker, an attentive one would not proceed
thinking like the cart driver.
Suppose a cart driver leaves the highway,
so even and well compacted.
They enter upon a rough road,
and fret as soon as their axle is broken.
So too, a dullard leaves the good
to follow what’s against the good.
Fallen in the jaws of death,
they fret like one whose axle is broken.”
Linked Discourses 2.23
3. Various Sectarians
With Serī

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho serī devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Serī addressed the Buddha in verse:
“Both gods and humans
enjoy their food.
So what’s the name of the spirit
who doesn’t like food?”
“Those who give with faith
and a clear and confident heart,
partake of food
in this world and the next.
So you should dispel stinginess,
overcoming that stain, and give a gift.
The good deeds of sentient beings
support them in the next world.”
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing,
how well said this was by the Buddha.” He repeated the Buddha’s verses, and said:

segs.p: Bhūtapubbāhaṁ, bhante, sirī nāma rājā ahosiṁ dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: “Once upon a time, sir, I was a king named Serī, a giver, a donor, who praised giving.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, catūsu dvāresu dānaṁ dīyittha samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavanibbakayācakānaṁ.
segs.e: I gave gifts at the four gates to ascetics and brahmins, to paupers, vagrants, supplicants, and beggars.

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, itthāgāraṁ upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the ladies of my harem approached me and said,

segs.p: ‘devassa kho dānaṁ dīyati; amhākaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati.
segs.e: ‘Your Majesty gives gifts, but we don’t.

segs.p: Sādhu mayampi devaṁ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: Your Majesty, please support us to give gifts and make merit.’
Then it occurred to me,
‘I’m a giver, a donor, who praises giving.
When they say, “We would give gifts”, what am I to say?’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, paṭhamaṁ dvāraṁ itthāgārassa adāsiṁ.
segs.e: And so I gave the first gate to the ladies of my harem.

segs.p: Tattha itthāgārassa dānaṁ dīyittha; mama dānaṁ paṭikkami.
segs.e: There they gave gifts, while my own giving dwindled.

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, khattiyā anuyantā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then my aristocrat vassals approached me and said,

segs.p: ‘devassa kho dānaṁ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṁ dīyati; amhākaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati.
segs.e: ‘Your Majesty gives gifts, the ladies of your harem give gifts, but we don’t.

segs.p: Sādhu mayampi devaṁ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: Your Majesty, please support us to give gifts and make merit.’
Then it occurred to me,
‘I’m a giver, a donor, who praises giving.
When they say, “We would give gifts”, what am I to say?’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, dutiyaṁ dvāraṁ khattiyānaṁ anuyantānaṁ adāsiṁ.
segs.e: And so I gave the second gate to my aristocrat vassals.

segs.p: Tattha khattiyānaṁ anuyantānaṁ dānaṁ dīyittha, mama dānaṁ paṭikkami.
segs.e: There they gave gifts, while my own giving dwindled.

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, balakāyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then my troops approached me and said,

segs.p: ‘devassa kho dānaṁ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṁ dīyati; khattiyānaṁ anuyantānaṁ dānaṁ dīyati; amhākaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati.
segs.e: ‘Your Majesty gives gifts, the ladies of your harem give gifts, your aristocrat vassals give gifts, but we don’t.

segs.p: Sādhu mayampi devaṁ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: Your Majesty, please support us to give gifts and make merit.’
Then it occurred to me,
‘I’m a giver, a donor, who praises giving.
When they say, “We would give gifts”, what am I to say?’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, tatiyaṁ dvāraṁ balakāyassa adāsiṁ.
segs.e: And so I gave the third gate to my troops.

segs.p: Tattha balakāyassa dānaṁ dīyittha, mama dānaṁ paṭikkami.
segs.e: There they gave gifts, while my own giving dwindled.

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, brāhmaṇagahapatikā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then my brahmins and householders approached me and said,

segs.p: ‘devassa kho dānaṁ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṁ dīyati; khattiyānaṁ anuyantānaṁ dānaṁ dīyati; balakāyassa dānaṁ dīyati; amhākaṁ dānaṁ na dīyati.
segs.e: ‘Your Majesty gives gifts, the ladies of your harem give gifts, your aristocrat vassals give gifts, your troops give gifts, but we don’t.

segs.p: Sādhu mayampi devaṁ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: Your Majesty, please support us to give gifts and make merit.’
Then it occurred to me,
‘I’m a giver, a donor, who praises giving.
When they say, “We would give gifts”, what am I to say?’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, catutthaṁ dvāraṁ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṁ adāsiṁ.
segs.e: And so I gave the fourth gate to my brahmins and householders.

segs.p: Tattha brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṁ dānaṁ dīyittha, mama dānaṁ paṭikkami.
segs.e: There they gave gifts, while my own giving dwindled.

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, bhante, purisā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then my men approached me and said,

segs.p: ‘na kho dāni devassa koci dānaṁ dīyatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now Your Majesty is not giving gifts anywhere!’

segs.p: Evaṁ vuttāhaṁ, bhante, te purise etadavocaṁ:
segs.e: When they said this, I said to those men,

segs.p: ‘tena hi, bhaṇe, yo bāhiresu janapadesu āyo sañjāyati tato upaḍḍhaṁ antepure pavesetha, upaḍḍhaṁ tattheva dānaṁ detha samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavanibbakayācakānan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Well then, lads, deposit half the revenue generated in the outer districts in the royal compound. Give the other half as charity to ascetics and brahmins, to paupers, vagrants, supplicants, and beggars in those districts.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ dīgharattaṁ katānaṁ puññānaṁ evaṁ dīgharattaṁ katānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pariyantaṁ nādhigacchāmi—
segs.e: Sir, for a long time I made so much merit and did so many skillful deeds. I never reached any limit so as to say

segs.p: ettakaṁ puññanti vā ettako puññavipākoti vā ettakaṁ sagge ṭhātabbanti vāti.
segs.e: ‘there’s this much merit’ or ‘there’s this much result of merit’ or ‘for so long I’ll remain in heaven’.
It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing,
how well said this was by the Buddha.
‘Those who give with faith
and a clear and confident heart,
partake of food
in this world and the next.
So you should dispel stinginess,
overcoming that stain, and give a gift.
The good deeds of sentient beings
support them in the next world.’”
Linked Discourses 2.24
3. Various Sectarians
With Ghaṭīkāra

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho ghaṭīkāro devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Ghaṭīkāra spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“Seven mendicants reborn in Aviha
have been freed.
With the complete ending of greed and hate,
they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”
“Who are those who’ve crossed the bog,
Death’s dominion so hard to pass?
Who, after leaving behind the human body,
have risen above celestial yokes?”
“Upaka and Palagaṇḍa,
and Pukkusāti, these three;
Bhaddiya and Bhaddadeva,
and Bāhudantī and Piṅgiya.
They, after leaving behind the human body,
have risen above celestial yokes.”
“You speak well of them,
who have let go the snares of Māra.
Whose teaching did they understand
to cut the bonds of rebirth?”
“None other than the Blessed One!
None other than your instruction!
It was your teaching that they understood
to cut the bonds of rebirth.
Where name and form
cease with no residue left behind;
understanding this teaching,
they cut the bonds of rebirth.”
“The words you say are deep,
hard to understand, so very hard to wake up to.
Whose teaching did you understand
to be able to say such things?”
“In the past I was a potter
in Vebhaliṅga named Ghaṭīkāra.
I took care of my parents
as a lay follower of Buddha Kassapa.
I refrained from sexual intercourse,
I was chaste, spiritual.
We lived in the same village;
in the past I was your comrade.
I am the one who understands
that these seven mendicants have been freed.
With the complete ending of greed and hate,
they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”
“That’s exactly how it was,
just as you say, Bhaggava.
In the past you were a potter
in Vebhaliṅga named Ghaṭīkāra.
You took care of your parents
as a lay follower of Buddha Kassapa.
You refrained from sexual intercourse,
you were chaste, spiritual.
We lived in the same village;
in the past you were my comrade.”
“That’s how it was
when those friends of old met again.
Both of them are evolved,
and bear their final body.”
Linked Discourses 2.25
3. Various Sectarians
With Jantu
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ sambahulā bhikkhū, kosalesu viharanti himavantapasse araññakuṭikāya uddhatā unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā muṭṭhassatino asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā pākatindriyā.
segs.e: At one time several mendicants were staying in the Kosalan lands, in a wilderness hut on the slopes of the Himalayas. They were haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

segs.p: Atha kho jantu devaputto tadahuposathe pannarase yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then on the fifteenth day sabbath the godling Jantu went up to those mendicants and addressed them in verse:
“The mendicants used to live happily,
as disciples of Gotama.
Desireless they sought alms;
desireless they used their lodgings.
Knowing that the world was impermanent
they made an end of suffering.
But now they’ve made themselves hard to look after,
like chiefs in a village.
They eat and eat and then lie down,
passed out in the homes of others.
Having raised my cupped palms to the Saṅgha,
I speak here only about certain people.
They’re dregs, with no protector,
just like those who have passed away.
I’m speaking about
those who live negligently.
To those who live diligently
I pay homage.”
Linked Discourses 2.26
3. Various Sectarians
With Rohitassa
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho rohitasso devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Rohitassa said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “yattha nu kho, bhante, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, sakkā nu kho so, bhante, gamanena lokassa anto ñātuṁ vā daṭṭhuṁ vā pāpuṇituṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, is it possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn?”

segs.p: “Yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṁ taṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ daṭṭheyyaṁ patteyyanti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Reverend, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.”
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing,
how well said this was by the Buddha.

segs.p: ‘yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṁ taṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ daṭṭheyyaṁ patteyyanti vadāmī’ti.
Bhūtapubbāhaṁ, bhante, rohitasso nāma isi ahosiṁ bhojaputto iddhimā vehāsaṅgamo.
segs.e: Once upon a time, I was a seer named Rohitassa, son of the benefactors. I was a sky-walker with psychic powers.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, evarūpo javo ahosi; seyyathāpi nāma daḷhadhammā dhanuggaho susikkhito katahattho katayoggo katūpāsano lahukena asanena appakasireneva tiriyaṁ tālacchāyaṁ atipāteyya.
segs.e: I was as fast as a light arrow easily shot across the shadow of a palm tree by a well-trained expert archer with a strong bow.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, evarūpo padavītihāro ahosi; seyyathāpi nāma puratthimā samuddā pacchimo samuddo.
segs.e: My stride was such that it could span from the eastern ocean to the western ocean.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, evarūpaṁ icchāgataṁ uppajji:
segs.e: This wish came to me:
‘I will reach the end of the world by traveling.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, evarūpena javena samannāgato evarūpena ca padavītihārena, aññatreva asitapītakhāyitasāyitā aññatra uccārapassāvakammā aññatra niddākilamathapaṭivinodanā vassasatāyuko vassasatajīvī vassasataṁ gantvā appatvāva lokassa antaṁ antarāva kālaṅkato.
segs.e: Having such speed and stride, I traveled for my whole lifespan of a hundred years—pausing only to eat and drink, go to the toilet, and sleep to dispel weariness—and I passed away along the way, never reaching the end of the world.
It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing,
how well said this was by the Buddha.

segs.p: ‘yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṁ taṁ gamanena lokassa antaṁ ñāteyyaṁ daṭṭheyyaṁ patteyyanti vadāmī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Reverend, I say it’s not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.’”

segs.p: “Na kho panāhaṁ, āvuso, appatvā lokassa antaṁ dukkhassa antakiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: “But Reverend, I also say there’s no making an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world.

segs.p: Api ca khvāhaṁ, āvuso, imasmiṁyeva byāmamatte kaḷevare sasaññimhi samanake lokañca paññapemi lokasamudayañca lokanirodhañca lokanirodhagāminiñca paṭipadanti.
segs.e: For it is in this fathom-long carcass with its perception and mind that I describe the world, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.
The end of the world can never
be reached by traveling.
But without reaching the end of the world,
there’s no release from suffering.
So an intelligent person, understanding the world,
has completed the spiritual journey <j>and gone to the end of the world.
Assuaged, knowing the end of the world,
they do not hope for this world or the next.”
Linked Discourses 2.27
3. Various Sectarians
With Nanda

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho nando devaputto bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Nanda spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“Time flies, nights pass by,
the stages of life leave us one by one.
Seeing this peril in death,
do good deeds that bring you joy.”
“Time flies, nights pass by,
the stages of life leave us one by one.
Seeing this peril in death,
a seeker of peace would drop the world’s bait.”
Linked Discourses 2.28
3. Various Sectarians
With Nandivisāla

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho nandivisālo devaputto bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Nandivisāla addressed the Buddha in verse:
“Four are its wheels, and nine its doors;
it’s stuffed full, bound with greed,
and born from a bog.
Great hero, how will I keep going?”
“Having cut the strap and harness—
wicked desire and greed—
and having plucked out craving, root and all:
that’s how you will keep going.”
Linked Discourses 2.29
3. Various Sectarians
With Susīma
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,
“Ānanda, do you endorse Sāriputta?”

segs.p: “Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya?
segs.e: “Sir, who on earth would not endorse Venerable Sāriputta unless they’re a fool, a hater, delusional, or mentally deranged?
Venerable Sāriputta is astute,
he has great wisdom,
widespread wisdom,
laughing wisdom,
swift wisdom,
sharp wisdom,
and penetrating wisdom.
He has few wishes,
he’s content,
secluded,
aloof,
and energetic.
He is a preacher,
and he accepts advice;
he accuses
and criticizes wickedness.

segs.p: Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?
segs.e: Who on earth would not endorse Venerable Sāriputta unless they’re a fool, a hater, delusional, or mentally deranged?”
“That’s so true, Ānanda! That’s so true!

segs.p: Kassa hi nāma, ānanda, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa sāriputto na rucceyya?
segs.e: Who on earth would not endorse Venerable Sāriputta unless they’re a fool, a hater, delusional, or mentally deranged?”
And the Buddha repeated all of Ānanda’s terms of praise.

segs.p: Kassa hi nāma, ānanda, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?

Atha kho susimo devaputto āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne mahatiyā devaputtaparisāya parivuto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho susimo devaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: While this praise of Sāriputta was being spoken, the godling Susīma approached the Buddha, escorted by a large assembly of godlings. He bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:
“That’s so true, Blessed One! That’s so true, Holy One!

segs.p: Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya?
segs.e: Who on earth would not endorse Venerable Sāriputta unless they’re a fool, a hater, delusional, or mentally deranged?”
And he too repeated all the terms of praise of Sāriputta, adding,

segs.p: Mahāpañño, bhante, puthupañño, bhante, hāsapañño, bhante, javanapañño, bhante, tikkhapañño, bhante, nibbedhikapañño, bhante, appiccho, bhante, santuṭṭho, bhante, pavivitto, bhante, asaṁsaṭṭho, bhante, āraddhavīriyo, bhante, vattā, bhante, vacanakkhamo, bhante, codako, bhante, pāpagarahī, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto.
Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya?
Ahampi hi, bhante, yaññadeva devaputtaparisaṁ upasaṅkamiṁ, etadeva bahulaṁ saddaṁ suṇāmi:
segs.e: “For I too, sir, whenever I go to an assembly of godlings, frequently hear the same terms of praise.”

segs.p: mahāpañño āyasmā, puthupañño āyasmā, hāsapañño āyasmā, javanapañño āyasmā, tikkhapañño āyasmā, nibbedhikapañño āyasmā, appiccho āyasmā, santuṭṭho āyasmā, pavivitto āyasmā, asaṁsaṭṭho āyasmā, āraddhavīriyo āyasmā, vattā āyasmā, vacanakkhamo āyasmā, codako āyasmā, pāpagarahī āyasmā sāriputto’ti.
Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?
Atha kho susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
segs.e: While this praise of Sāriputta was being spoken, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly—uplifted and overjoyed, full of rapture and happiness—displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṁso suparikammakato paṇḍukambale nikkhitto bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca;
segs.e: Suppose there was a beryl gem that was naturally lustrous, eight-faceted, well-worked. When placed on a cream rug it would sine and glow and dazzle.

segs.p: evamevaṁ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
segs.e: In the same way, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma nikkhaṁ jambonadaṁ dakkhakammāraputtaukkāmukhasukusalasampahaṭṭhaṁ paṇḍukambale nikkhittaṁ bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca;
segs.e: Suppose there was a pendant of Black Plum River gold, fashioned by a deft smith, well wrought in the forge. When placed on a cream rug it would shine and glow and dazzle.

segs.p: evamevaṁ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
segs.e: In the same way, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ osadhitārakā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca;
segs.e: Suppose that in the autumn the heavens were clear and cloudless. At the crack of dawn, the morning star shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: evamevaṁ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
segs.e: In the same way, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nabhaṁ abbhussakkamāno sabbaṁ ākāsagataṁ tamagataṁ abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca;
segs.e: Suppose that in the autumn the heavens were clear and cloudless. As the sun is rising to the firmament, having dispelled all the darkness of space, shines and glows and dazzles.

segs.p: evamevaṁ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṁseti.
segs.e: In the same way, the godlings of Susīma’s assembly displayed a rainbow of bright colors.

segs.p: Atha kho susimo devaputto āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then the godling Susīma spoke this verse about Venerable Sāriputta in the Buddha’s presence:
“He’s considered astute,
Sāriputta, free of anger.
Few in wishes, gentle, tamed,
the seer shines in the Teacher’s praise!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ ārabbha susimaṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha replied to Susīma with this verse about Venerable Sāriputta:
“He’s considered astute,
Sāriputta, free of anger.
Few in wishes, gentle, tamed;
developed and well-tamed, he awaits his time.”
Linked Discourses 2.30
3. Various Sectarians
The Disciples of Various Monastics of Other Religions
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā nānātitthiyasāvakā devaputtā asamo ca sahali ca nīko ca ākoṭako ca vegabbhari ca māṇavagāmiyo ca abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ veḷuvanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
segs.e: Then, late at night, several glorious godlings lit up the entire Bamboo Grove. They were Asama, Sahalī, Niṅka, Ākoṭaka, Veṭambarī, and Māṇavagāmiya, and all of them were disciples of various monastics of other religions. They went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho asamo devaputto pūraṇaṁ kassapaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Standing to one side, the godling Asama spoke this verse about Pūraṇa Kassapa in the Buddha’s presence:
“In injuring and killing here,
in beating and extortion,
Kassapa saw no evil,
nor any merit for oneself.
What he taught should truly be trusted,
he’s worthy of esteem as Teacher.”

segs.p: Atha kho sahali devaputto makkhaliṁ gosālaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then the godling Sahalī spoke this verse about the bamboo-staffed ascetic Gosāla in the Buddha’s presence:
“Through fervent mortification in disgust of sin he became well restrained.
He gave up quarreling with people.
Refraining from false speech, he spoke the truth.

segs.p: Na hi nūna tādisaṁ karoti pāpan”ti.
segs.e: Surely such a man does no wrong!”

segs.p: Atha kho nīko devaputto nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then the godling Niṅka spoke this verse about the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan in the Buddha’s presence:
“Disgusted at sin, an alert mendicant,
well restrained in the fourfold constraint;
explaining what is seen and heard:
surely he can be no sinner!”

segs.p: Atha kho ākoṭako devaputto nānātitthiye ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then the godling Ākoṭaka spoke this verse about various sectarian teachers in the Buddha’s presence:
“Pakudhaka Kātiyāna and the Jain ascetic,
as well as this bamboo-staffed ascetic and Pūraṇa:
Teachers of communities, attained ascetics,

segs.p: Na hi nūna te sappurisehi dūre”ti.
segs.e: surely they weren’t far from truly good men!”

segs.p: Atha kho vegabbhari devaputto ākoṭakaṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the godling Veṭambarī replied to the godling Ākoṭaka in verse:
“Though the wretched jackal howls along,
it never equals the lion.
A nude liar with suspicious conduct,
though they teach a community, is not like the good.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā begabbhariṁ devaputtaṁ anvāvisitvā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked took possession of the godling Veṭambarī and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“Those dedicated to mortification in disgust of sin,
safeguarding their seclusion,
entrenched in form,
they rejoice in the heavenly realm.
Indeed, those mortals give correct instructions
regarding the next world.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā, māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāya paccabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

segs.p: “Ye keci rūpā idha vā huraṁ vā,
segs.e: “Whatever forms there are in this life or the next,
and those of shining beauty in the sky,
all of these you praise, Namuci,
like bait tossed out for catching fish.”

segs.p: Atha kho māṇavagāmiyo devaputto bhagavantaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: Then the godling Māṇavagāmiya spoke this verse about the Buddha in his presence:
“Of all the mountains of Rājagaha,
Vepulla’s said to be the best.
Seta is the best of the Himalayan peaks,
and the sun, of travelers in space.
The ocean is the best of seas,
and the moon, of lights that shine at night.
But in all the world with its gods,
the Buddha is declared foremost.”
The Linked Discourses on Godlings are complete.
